newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU refinery output down, but distillates up in Oct.
newsitem.headline: EU refinery output down, but distillates up in Oct.

text.p: Middle distillate output in the European Union rose 1.2 percent in October, while total net refinery output was down 1.0 percent, Stichting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.

Middle distillate output in the 14 nations of the European Union, excluding Sweden, was up 62,000 barrels per day (1.2 percent) in October at 5.347 million barrels per day (bpd). The rise was not concentrated in any one country.

Total refinery output fell 124,000 bpd (1.0 percent) to 11.715 million bpd in October, while refinery crude intake was down 306,000 bpd (2.7 percent) to 11.009 million bpd. This represented a utilisation rate of 87.37 percent, against 89.80 percent in September.
But year-on-year, total output was up 192,000 bpd (1.7 percent).
Gasoline production fell 34,000 bpd (1.1 percent) in October to 3.172 million bpd, but this was 10,000 bpd (0.3 percent) more than in October 1995.
Naphtha output was up 13,000 bpd (1.5 percent) to 908,000 bpd, 32,000 bpd (3.7 percent) higher than a year ago.
Fuel oil output was down 1.6 percent at 1.617 million bpd.
They are based on a nameplate capacity of 12.6 million bpd. Refinery intake represents crude only and excludes natural gas liquids, feedstocks and other inputs.
